summary:
Description:
Tango Horizon is a real-time 3D simulator of Mars mission operations, robotics and weather. It runs on real NASA/USGS Gale Crater topography and imagery. A multi-agent SI (super intelligence) system orchestrates the mission and protects the astronauts, with a Run-Time Assurance guardrail (GUARDIAN) checking every action before it runs.

- Hands-free voice: commands in 5 languages.
- Autonomous rescue: the orchestrator sends robots to the casualty and delivers life support to the required position.
- 7 agentic robots and drones: each one takes voice orders from the astronaut or from the base orchestrator. The manipulator rover uses analytical inverse kinematics and multimodal vision to find rocks and drill them.
- In-memory RAG in under 2 ms: it searches NASA-STD-3001 to predict astronaut health, schedule MOXIE maintenance and raise radiation alerts.
- 3 trained ML models: subsurface water-ice prediction from orbital data, Storm Nowcaster for dust storms, and a vein detector for evidence of past water.
details:
What it does and how it works

Tango Horizon is a real-time 3D simulator of Mars surface operations. It runs at 60 FPS in the browser over real NASA/USGS cartography of Gale Crater (HiRISE/CTX elevation, THEMIS thermal data, MSL DAN hydrogen readings and Curiosity photos). On top of the terrain sits a 20-module base, four astronauts and seven robots and drones. A deterministic physics core computes the numbers: Pandolf metabolic rate, suit leak flow, RK4 ballistics, radiation dose from sky view, solar power and route planning.

A multi-agent AI system runs the mission:

- BASE is the orchestrator. It puts crew survival ahead of science and delegates to specialist agents for health, EVA planning, science, weather/radiation and maintenance.

- Every robot and drone is its own agent. The astronaut can command each one by voice, or the base orchestrator can.

- Every action the AI proposes passes through GUARDIAN, a Run-Time Assurance layer. Deterministic hard limits come first: vehicle slope limits, a 15 m keep-out radius around the pod and a 2 m arm keep-out from the crew. An AI safety judge reviews the action second.

- The agents use tools. They call six in-process MCP servers (terrain, suit, environment, fleet, HUD and knowledge) that compute exact numbers from the shared physics core instead of estimating them.

- The RAG runs in memory. It searches NASA-SSA medical briefs in under 2 ms and returnsdocument and page citations. It supports astronaut health prediction, MOXIE predictive maintenance and radiation alerts.

l is 100% hands-free. Voice works in English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. Critical commands run locally in under 5 ms, and the rest go to the agents. A phone can act as a pointer through a WebSocket link.

The main scenario is an autonomous rescue. An astronaut is incapacitated in a pit during a dust storm. The orchestrator raises the emergency alert, dispatches a rescue rover, overwatch drones and a rescue robot, and sends life support to the required position. If the cloud AI is unreachable, the system falls back to deterministic rule-based execution, so the mission keeps running.

The manipulator rover is not a mock. It solves analytical inverse kinematics for its arm and uses multimodal vision on

its camera feed to find rocks and drill them

We also trained three machine learning models:

- Hydration Prospector: predicts subsurface water ice from orbital data, validated against real DAN measurements.

- Storm Nowcaster: forecasts dust storms 3 sols ahead with an uncertainty band and a Go/No-Go verdict for EVA.

- Vein Detector: a vision model that flags evidence of past water in Curiosity images.

Benefits and intended impact

Communication with Mars has a delay of many to act without waiting for Earth. The project shows how a crew-support AI can respond to emergencies on its own while staying safe. Every action is checked by hard mits, every medical or radiation claim citmodel reports its uncertainty. The samearchitecture can support mission planning, crew training and the study of Moon and Mars surface operations. It also makes this kind of mission readable to the public.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

Languages and frontend: TypeScript, Three. for the data pipeline and model training.

- Backend: Node.js with Fastify, and a shared physics and types package (@th/shared).

- AI: Gemini models on Google Cloud Vertex AI, with the Gemini API and Meta Muse as automatic failover; Model Context Protocol (MCP); in-memory BM25 retrieval; e Cloud Text-to-Speech and the Web SpeechAPI.

- Data: NASA/USGS HiRISE, CTX, THEMIS, MRO, MSL DAN and RAD, MOXIE, DONKI space weather, JPL Horizons, and CuriMastcam/MAHLI images.

- Deployment: Google Cloud Run, Vercel, Terraform and Google Secret Manager. Assets: 3D models made by the team and opt

- Hardware: only a standard computer and a phone; there is no custom hardware.

- Showcase site: a Next.js editorial site.

Creativity

The agents and the physics are separate. T computes, so numbers are never made up.

- Safety comes from a Run-Time Assurance layer that combines deterministic limits with an AI judge, instead of trusting the model alone.

- Every robot is an autonomous agent that can still be commanded by voice.

- The sources are real NASA data: terrain, a and medical standards.

- The simulator is also a product demo: a full rescue is scripted and recorded as scenes.

Factors the team considered

- Safety: an AI that moves vehicles and armss that do not depend on the model.

three-provider failover and the offline fallback.

- Latency: local voice intents, in-process MCP and in-memory RAG keep responses fast.

- Data accuracy: we cite the source of every dataset. Where we use a design assumption, such as some bio-twin relations, we label it as an assumption.

- Model limits: the Storm Nowcaster band covers less than its nominal 80% on held-out data, and we report that.

- Accessibility: five languages and hands-fr astronaut cannot use their hands.

- Reach: the simulator runs in the browser with no installation, so anyone can try it.
